newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - ABP sees more investment in 97.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - ABP sees more investment in 97.

text.p: Associated British Ports Plc, which reported a 5.8 percent rise in year pretax profits earlier on Wednesday, said it planned to pump more money into facilities in 1997, but said it was unlikely that investment would top 1996 levels.

Charles Orange, finance director, told Reuters in an interview: "We will see more in 1997 which will be another high investment year. For 1998 onwards we do have some projects which are still in the planning stage but which have not yet been approved."
Those included riverside projects in north east England's Hull and Immingham, he said.

Capital expenditure for 1996 was 83 million stg. The group reported year pre-tax profits of 93.5 million stg earlier, after accounting for a three million charge related to its exit from a pipe-coating joint venture in Humberside.
Orange said: "It's made losses over the last couple of years and stood out as a non-core business."
He said the outlook for the group looked sound provided the UK economy continued to show stable growth.

On the issue of the recent strength in stg, he said there had been no net impact as any fall in UK exports would be balanced by more imports. "Also, since we bill and pay in sterling, it hasn't affected our profit."

On the subject of the opposition Labour Party's threat to impose a windfall tax on privatised utilities -- a move which some commentators say will include ABP -- Orange said he believed the company would not be hit.
"We don't think we're liable. We are not a monopoly and we are not a utility, so we should not be included."
Labour is expected to win the next election which must be held by May 22.
